hints: Focus on reversing addition polymerisation by joining the two backbone carbons with a C=C double bond.
The monomer has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so count the longest chain containing the double bond.
Compare the positions of the two higher priority ethyl groups across the double bond to decide if the isomer is cis or trans.
walkthrough:
**Recover the monomer from the repeat unit**

Think like a teacher undoing the polymerisation. In addition polymerisation the C=C double bond opens to make two new C-C single bonds.

To go backwards, erase the outer bonds and put the double bond back:
$$-\text{C}-\text{C}- \rightarrow \text{C}=\text{C}$$
So the monomer is:
$$\text{(C}_2\text{H}_5\text{)(CH}_3\text{)C}=\text{C(CH}_3\text{)(C}_2\text{H}_5\text{)}$$

**Name the carbon skeleton correctly**

Now find the longest chain through the double bond. Each side is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=$.

That gives a 6-carbon chain with the double bond starting at C3, plus a methyl on C3 and on C4:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{C(CH}_3\text{)}=\text{C(CH}_3\text{)}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
This is 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene. A 5-carbon pent-2-ene name misses one carbon, and a 1,2-diethyl-1,2-dimethyl ethene name does not use the longest chain.

**Assign cis or trans**

Look at the diagram positions. On the left C the $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ is up and $\text{CH}_3$ is down. On the right C the $\text{CH}_3$ is up and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ is down.

For each C=C carbon, ethyl has higher priority than methyl. Here the two high priority ethyl groups are on opposite sides of the double bond, one up and one down. Opposite sides means trans, so the monomer is trans-3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene.

options.A: This describes the same atoms but it is not the preferred IUPAC name because it does not use the longest 6-carbon chain, and it states cis. The two ethyl groups are on opposite sides in the diagram, so cis is wrong.
options.B: 2-ethyl-3-methylpent-2-ene uses a 5-carbon parent instead of the correct 6-carbon hexene parent. It also states cis, but the two ethyl groups are trans to each other.
options.C: This correctly spots the trans geometry but keeps the wrong carbon skeleton. The longest chain through the double bond is six carbons, not five, so it should be a dimethylhexene not an ethylmethylpentene.
options.D: The monomer reformed from the repeat unit is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(CH}_3\text{)}=\text{C(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene. The two higher priority ethyl groups are on opposite sides, giving the trans isomer.
